headline: Brewers rout Rays 10–1, one win from first World Series title

top.headline: Brewers rout Rays 10–1, one win from first World Series title
top.summary: Milwaukee beat Tampa Bay 10–1 at Tropicana Field on Monday to take a 3–0 World Series lead, leaving the Brewers one win from the first title in franchise history. They scored eight runs with two outs in the fifth inning, with seven straight batters getting hits. Robert Gasser threw six scoreless innings and allowed one hit, and Jackson Chourio went 4-for-5. Game 4 is Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET in Tampa Bay.

top.headline: Thunder lose Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace to surgery
top.summary: Jalen Williams will have surgery for a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, and Cason Wallace for a torn labrum in his left shoulder, after both were hurt in Sunday's win over the Clippers. GM Sam Presti said both are out indefinitely, and both are expected to miss several months, if not the entire season.

top.headline: Cowboys run past Eagles 38–21 on Monday night
top.summary: Javonte Williams ran for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes as Dallas snapped a two-game skid to reach 3–4. Philadelphia, starting Tanner McKee with Jalen Hurts out, lost its fifth straight to fall to 2–5. Saquon Barkley left with a back injury in his return from a hamstring injury.

stories.headline: Unbeaten Vikings climb to No. 1 in power rankings
stories.summary: Minnesota (6–0), the league's last unbeaten team, took the top spot in Pete Prisco's Week 8 rankings at CBS Sports after a 16–10 win over the Colts. NFL.com also moved the Vikings to No. 1, while ESPN kept the 6–1 49ers on top and FOX put the Bills first.

stories.headline: Jerry Jones open to a deadline deal but calls it unlikely
stories.summary: After the win in Philadelphia, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that he would make a significant trade-deadline acquisition if one came along. He called such a deal unlikely for now because few teams are looking to sell good players. The trade deadline is Nov. 10.

stories.headline: 49ers optimistic McCaffrey's hamstring is minor
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey hurt his hamstring in San Francisco's Week 7 loss to Atlanta. Per 49ers insider Cam Inman, Kyle Shanahan is optimistic he will play in Week 9 against the Raiders after this week's bye. If he can't, rookie Kaelon Black would lead the backfield.

standouts.name: Javonte Williams
standouts.note: A career high and Dallas's first 150-yard rushing game since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018, powering a 204-yard ground attack in the win at Philadelphia.

standouts.name: Joe Burrow
standouts.note: All four touchdown passes came after halftime as Cincinnati erased a 13–0 deficit and routed Baltimore 35–13.

standouts.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
standouts.note: Led Seattle's 20–3 Sunday night win that handed Kansas City its first loss of the season.

stories.headline: Edwards scores 47, but Cavs win in overtime
stories.summary: Anthony Edwards scored 47 points, but Cleveland beat Minnesota 127-125 in overtime. Donovan Mitchell scored 26, including a go-ahead 19-foot fadeaway with 48 seconds left in OT, and second-round rookie Meleek Thomas added 16 in his NBA debut.

stories.headline: Perfect Curry, rookie Lendeborg give Warriors first win
stories.summary: Stephen Curry went 8-for-8 from the field for 24 points, and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 31 points, 12 rebounds and 6 assists as Golden State won 134-114 at Denver. It was the Warriors' first win of the season.

stories.headline: Heat fall to 0–4 despite Giannis triple-double
stories.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo had 29 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists, his first triple-double since joining Miami, but the Heat gave up a fourth-quarter lead and lost 113-109 to Dallas. Cooper Flagg had 29 points, 11 assists, 5 steals and 3 blocks for the Mavericks after missing a game with a shoulder strain.

stories.headline: Brandon Miller pours in career-high 39
stories.summary: Brandon Miller scored a career-high 39 points with 6 rebounds, 3 steals and 2 blocks as Charlotte beat Washington 110-103. Moussa Diabate added 11 points and 17 rebounds, 11 of them offensive.

standouts.name: Anthony Edwards
standouts.note: Hit 5 of 15 threes in a 127-125 overtime loss at Cleveland, his seventh career game of 47 or more points.

standouts.name: Brandon Miller
standouts.note: Career high on 15-of-28 shooting, with five 3-pointers, in a 110-103 win over Washington.

standouts.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
standouts.note: The rookie went 12 of 13 at the line as Golden State routed Denver for its first win.

leagues.name: NHL
leagues.summary: Matthews reaches 800 points, but the Flames win

stories.headline: Matthews hits 800 points faster than any Maple Leaf, but Flames win
stories.summary: Auston Matthews assisted on William Nylander's goal for his 800th career point in his 703rd game, the fastest in Maple Leafs history (Darryl Sittler needed 742). It came in a 5-2 loss in Calgary, where Matvei Gridin scored twice and the Flames won their fourth straight. Toronto's four-game winning streak ended.

stories.headline: Postava wins NHL debut start as Red Wings top Oilers in shootout
stories.summary: Michal Postava made 25 saves and stopped all three Edmonton shootout attempts in his first NHL start, and Lucas Raymond scored the only shootout goal in Detroit's 4-3 win. Dylan Larkin tied it 3-3 late in the third with the goalie pulled. Connor McDavid had an assist, extending his season-opening point streak to 12 games, and Zach Hyman left in the second period and did not return.

stories.headline: Doughty's three points lead Kings past Rangers at MSG
stories.summary: Drew Doughty had a goal and two assists, his first three-point game since Feb. 22, 2025, as Los Angeles won 6-3 at Madison Square Garden for its third win in four games. James Reimer, in his first start since signing with New York, allowed three goals on eight shots and was pulled in the first period. The Rangers (7-6-1) have lost three straight.

stories.headline: Quinn Hughes hits 500 points in his return to Vancouver
stories.summary: Quinn Hughes was booed in his first game back in Vancouver since the December 2025 trade, then scored a power-play goal on Sunday for his 500th NHL point, in his 520th game. He added an assist in the Wild's 4-2 win. Only Brian Leetch reached 500 points faster among American defensemen.

stories.headline: Kraken lose McCann for 10 weeks; Hall could return for Carolina
stories.summary: Seattle forward Jared McCann (lower body) was placed on injured reserve and will be out 10 weeks. Carolina's Taylor Hall came off injured reserve and could return from an upper-body injury against Boston on Tuesday. Philadelphia's Rasmus Ristolainen is expected to miss at least two weeks.

standouts.name: Matvei Gridin
standouts.note: First three-point game of his NHL career, including a power-play goal, as Calgary won its fourth straight.

standouts.name: Drew Doughty
standouts.note: His first goal of the season moved him past Dustin Brown into seventh on the Kings' all-time points list (713).

standouts.name: Michal Postava
standouts.note: Won his first NHL start, stopping all three Edmonton shooters in the shootout.

stories.headline: Lindor wins 2026 Roberto Clemente Award
stories.summary: Mets shortstop Francisco Lindor was named the 2026 Roberto Clemente Award winner on Monday. The award goes to one player each season for philanthropic work. His work includes money for disaster relief in Puerto Rico and a partnership with New Balance that provides school supplies for students.

stories.headline: Mariners bring Espada, Kanzler in for in-person manager interviews
stories.summary: Seattle is holding in-person interviews this week with former Astros manager Joe Espada and Cubs player development director Jason Kanzler. This is the third round of talks for both candidates. Rocco Baldelli was scheduled for an in-person interview but withdrew over the weekend for family reasons. The Mariners have been searching for a manager since they parted ways with Dan Wilson after the regular season.

stories.headline: Phillies hire ex-Red Sox hitting coach Peter Fatse
stories.summary: According to The Athletic's sources, the Phillies are hiring Peter Fatse as their hitting coach to replace Kevin Long. Fatse was with the Red Sox from 2019 until April 2026, when Boston let him go in the staff shakeup that also removed manager Alex Cora. He then worked as a hitting consultant for the Rays.
